beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The same addition sign can hide different rules in different mathematical environments.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ideal integers and fixed-width machine integers do not have identical operational behavior.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: In eight-bit unsigned wraparound arithmetic, adding one to 255 gives zero.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Checked arithmetic would instead reject an overflow under its specified operation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An ideal integer calculation can continue to 256 without that implementation restriction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book uses this contrast to separate structure, representation, and implementation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A transferred theorem needs a bridge that preserves the property being claimed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This small example makes the larger research question concrete before the architecture expands.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The programme does not reduce mathematical proof to repeatedly running examples.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Finite derivations can establish general results without enumerating every possible input.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks how witnesses, counterexamples, invariants, and bounded results should be represented.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Different analysis techniques may establish different properties with different scopes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their names alone do not tell us what a particular result closes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A common evidence structure would preserve assumptions, coverage, and the trusted basis.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a way to compare methods without flattening them into one verdict.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The detailed chapters explore how their outputs might compose without silently strengthening claims.
